## Episode Thesis

Lars Thylander, a Danish real-estate investor, is the guest. He says his fund focuses on residential property in Greater Copenhagen and on data centres, because demand in both is far larger than supply. He stresses location, moderate leverage (about 60% mortgage-credit financing) and stable cash flow. The hosts discuss the Iran/Hormuz conflict: they think oil peaked near $100 but see no quick rate relief. Thylander sees the Danish housing market cooling, is bullish on data centres and prime Copenhagen offices, and says to stay away from provincial rentals.
